record.paper_title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
record.original_question: Let X1 and X2 be smooth projective varieties over a field, in the same deformation class, and suppose their Kuznetsov components Ku(X1) and Ku(X2) are equivalent. Must X1 and X2 be birational?

evidence.quote: Is it true that if Ku(X_1) and Ku(X_2) are equivalent

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be smooth projective varieties defined over a field $k$, and assume that $X_1$ and $X_2$ belong to the same deformation class (i.e., they are deformation equivalent as smooth projective varieties). For a smooth projective variety $X$ in a class admitting a semiorthogonal decomposition of its bounded derived category $D^b(X)$ of coherent sheaves of the form
$$D^b(X) = \langle \mathcal{K}u(X), E_1, \dots, E_n \rangle,$$
where $E_1, \dots, E_n$ is an exceptional collection and $\mathcal{K}u(X)$ is the right orthogonal admissible subcategory (the Kuznetsov component), suppose there exists a $k$-linear exact equivalence
$$\mathcal{K}u(X_1) \simeq \mathcal{K}u(X_2).$$
Must $X_1$ and $X_2$ be birational over $k$?
artifact.status_search_result: The birational categorical Torelli problem for Kuznetsov components is a general open conjecture. Specific instances have been verified: for example, for Gushel–Mukai threefolds (where the Categorical Torelli fails up to isomorphism but birationality has been established in important cases) and for various Fano threefolds, partial and conditional results are known. In full generality (smooth projective varieties in a fixed deformation class) the question remains open.
